subject.title: [Feature]: define shared application surfaces for macOS and Control UI

question: Should Carapace add an opt-in application-anatomy candidate contract now, or should the macOS and Control UI teams continue refining these layouts locally until a smaller shared contract is demonstrated?
rationale: This is a new product and scope decision, not a repair to an established shared contract. The repository policy supports common behavior shared by multiple consumers but reserves consumer-specific components and layouts for their own repositories.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded candidate contract
options.body: Add only framework-neutral shared anatomy with two-consumer reference evidence and keep consumer lifecycle, routing, and native chrome out of Carapace.

options.title: Defer to consumer implementations
options.body: Keep the patterns local until concrete adoption identifies a smaller, stable common contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded candidate contract
recommendation.body: Add only framework-neutral shared anatomy with two-consumer reference evidence and keep consumer lifecycle, routing, and native chrome out of Carapace.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the only repository-connected person identified in the supplied context and authored the proposed cross-consumer scope.
